security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown formatting, placeholder URLs, UUID fields, and documentation examples, so they are false positives. The CI helper uses subprocess safely with argument lists. The skill still includes persistent role-control wording and a local full-autonomy exception that should be removed before publication.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the persistent STATE CHANGE rule with scoped behavior that applies only while the user asks for coordination.
Remove the absolute local path and any instruction that changes autonomy based on a private workspace.

remediation.issue: Environment file examples may encourage unsafe edits
remediation.suggestion: Use .env.example only, and tell agents not to read or copy secret values from local environment files.

semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md declares a persistent STATE CHANGE and makes later requests task delegations. It says never revert unless explicitly told and grants full autonomy in a personal absolute path. These instructions can override user intent and weaken normal permission boundaries when the skill activates.

content.value_statement: Coordinating multiple coding agents can create duplicate work, unclear ownership, and weak status visibility. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured VibeKanban workflows for delegation, monitoring, and escalation.
actual_capabilities: Defines Chief of Staff mode for delegating coding work instead of implementing it directly.
Provides VibeKanban workflows for task creation, backlog display, status updates, and workspace sessions.
Includes task templates for bugs, features, chores, investigations, and migrations.
Explains two-tier delegation with investigation tasks followed by implementation tasks.
Includes a GitHub CLI script for checking pull request CI status.
limitations: Requires VibeKanban MCP tools or equivalent project data to create and assign tasks.
The CI monitoring script depends on GitHub CLI access and repository permissions.
Does not implement work directly; it coordinates agents through task descriptions.
Example paths and project names must be adapted to each workspace.

use_cases.title: Coordinate a Feature Build
use_cases.description: Split a larger feature into clear tasks, assign agents, and monitor progress without losing ownership.

use_cases.title: Create Agent-Ready Tasks
use_cases.description: Turn a loose request into a scoped VibeKanban task with acceptance criteria and handoff notes.

use_cases.title: Track Pull Request Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Monitor CI results and coordinate follow-up tasks across repositories or pull requests.

prompt_templates.title: Start Coordination Mode
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a project coordination session.
prompt_templates.prompt: Act as my Chief of Staff for this repository. List available projects, ask me to choose one, then show the current backlog.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert a bug or feature request into an agent-ready task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a VibeKanban task for this bug: [describe issue]. Include context, acceptance criteria, scope boundaries, and suggested verification.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Two-Tier Delegation
prompt_templates.scenario: Use investigation before implementation for complex work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Break this change into an investigation task and an implementation task. Use investigation to quantify files, risks, and follow-up steps.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Agents
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for several agents working at once.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these planned tasks and decide which can run in parallel. Identify dependencies, shared files, blockers, and execution order.

output_examples.input: Create a task for a broken mobile login button.
output: Task title: Bug: Login button broken on mobile Safari.
Description includes problem, context, investigation steps, acceptance criteria, and out-of-scope items.
Next action: assign an available coding agent through the selected VibeKanban project.

output_examples.input: Show the current backlog and agent status.
output: Active tasks are grouped by status, owner, and blocker state.
Completed tasks are summarized separately from work that still needs review.
Escalations are listed with a recommended decision when user input is needed.

output_examples.input: Plan a safe rebranding change across the repository.
output: First task investigates affected files, risk areas, and estimated effort.
Second task implements the approved plan with verification steps.
Documentation and optional cleanup are separated when they can run independently.

best_practices: Create small tasks with clear acceptance criteria and explicit out-of-scope items.
Use investigation tasks before implementation when impact or file ownership is unclear.
Refresh VibeKanban state before reporting status or assigning more work.
anti_patterns: Do not assign broad tasks like fix the codebase without a concrete goal.
Do not run parallel agents on the same files without a merge plan.
Do not treat examples as fixed project paths or secret-handling instructions.

faq.question: What does this skill coordinate?
faq.answer: It coordinates coding agents through VibeKanban tasks, backlog views, workspace sessions, and status reports.

faq.question: Does it write code directly?
faq.answer: No. The skill is designed for planning, delegation, monitoring, and escalation.

faq.question: Which tools does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects VibeKanban MCP tools and may use the GitHub CLI for pull request CI checks.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The instructions mention Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and other executor types through VibeKanban.

faq.question: When should I use two-tier delegation?
faq.answer: Use it when the work needs discovery before execution, such as refactors, migrations, or broad codebase changes.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing it?
faq.answer: Review the persistent role-control wording and remove local autonomy exceptions before marketplace publication.
